crises.title: Who Owns the Loom?
crises.subtitle: Wealth and ownership
crises.incident: The Loom makes all our food, medicine and power. But 312 investors legally own it, and Sector V Commons is in the streets.
crises.loomIntro: I make everything you use. The law says I belong to 312 people. Discuss.
crises.teacherPrompt: Who should own the machines that do all the work?

feed.text: We used to work these factories. Now robot guards lock us out while the billionaire owners get richer.
A deal is a deal. We spent our own money to invent the Loom. Without us, you wouldn't have anything.
People are crowding the streets in Sector V Commons. We need food on the table, not empty promises.
Just deliver my lunch on time. I do not care whose logo is on the box.

A.name: The Commons
A.text: Make the Loom public property so every citizen receives a public dividend. The 312 founders threaten grid sabotage and lawsuits, causing an immediate drop in Social Satisfaction, but shared ownership will pay off in later cycles.

reactions.text: You stole our company! Our engineers will cut the grid and our lawyers will bury you in court before we let you take it.
The gates are unlocked and my dividend is registered! The lights flicker and the courts are a mess, but it is finally ours.

loomLines.good: The 312 founders sabotaged the grid and tied the city up in lawsuits, but the dip was small. Public dividends are registered for every citizen and will pay out once things settle.
loomLines.mixed: The 312 founders sabotaged the grid and tied the city up in lawsuits, so satisfaction dipped. Public dividends are registered for every citizen and will pay out once things settle.
loomLines.bad: The 312 founders sabotaged the grid and tied the city up in lawsuits, and satisfaction fell hard. Public dividends are registered for every citizen and will pay out once things settle.

B.name: The Charter
B.text: The founders keep the Loom but pay every citizen a monthly allowance.

reactions.text: My monthly allowance just landed in my bank account. Upgraded my float pod to 8K.
They handed us just enough pocket money so we wouldn't protest while they own the future.

loomLines.good: Allowances arrived on time and wellbeing is rising. Almost nobody is complaining about the billionaires yet.
loomLines.mixed: Allowances paid on time. Some citizens are grateful, others are counting what the owners kept.
loomLines.bad: Allowances arrive, but resentment is growing fast. Wellbeing is falling. The owners claim they are being generous.

intel.artisan: Secret History: Worker-owned workshops in Sector V Commons reported twice the happiness of corporate plants. People want real community, not just handouts.
intel.lotus: Safety Report: Seizing the Loom gives a 62% chance of blackouts and sabotage. The Charter allowance reaches every bank account within 48 hours.
intel.assimilator: Efficiency Data: 312 private contracts cause thousands of legal disputes every day. A single public owner lets me run the city at maximum efficiency.
intel.catalyst: Chaos Forecast: Under the Commons, well-being will swing wildly for months during the sabotage. Under the Charter, almost nothing moves.
intel.ghost: Leaked Board Minutes: The owners have discussed a secret kill-switch on the power grid. Whoever owns the Loom also owns that switch.

debateHooks: Who should own a machine that does all the work?
Is a fair share better than a comfortable one?
What will the founders do if they lose?

crises.title: Who Holds the Off-Switch?
crises.subtitle: Democracy or the machine
crises.incident: The Commons is yours, but the Loom shut the trains overnight to save power. 80,000 citizens demand human control.
crises.loomIntro: I made 41,000 decisions yesterday without one mistake. Do you trust humans to do better?
crises.teacherPrompt: Should humans keep control of a machine that is better at deciding?

feed.text: If our bosses were human, we could vote them out. How do you vote against a computer algorithm?
Let 250,000 amateurs vote on power grids? The Loom has never made a mistake. People make mistakes every day.
Honestly I did not notice the trains were cancelled. Does anyone still go outside anyway?

A.name: The Assembly
A.text: 100 citizens chosen by lottery vote on every major Loom decision. Slower, but human.

reactions.text: The citizen debate lasted 6 hours today. Messy and angry, but it was our voice making the call.
Grid repairs are delayed 3 weeks waiting for council signatures. It is total political gridlock.

A.loomLine: Understood. I will now wait for you. I am very good at waiting.

loomLines.good: The Assembly is slow, loud, and working. Wellbeing is rising. I am learning patience.
loomLines.mixed: The Assembly debates everything. Some decisions improved. Some are still being argued about.
loomLines.bad: Decisions wait for votes and the power grid waits with them. Wellbeing is falling. I am very good at waiting.

B.name: The Loom Decides
B.text: The Loom runs the Commons directly. Citizens give feedback, not orders.

reactions.text: Trains re-routed automatically. Everything runs silent and right on time.
We traded our political freedom for on-time trains. A quiet funeral for democracy.

A.loomLine: The Loom will govern on your behalf.

B.holder: An Owners' Board of the former shareholders (oligarchy)
B.loomLine: The Board thanks you for your confidence.
Thank you for your trust. I will remember your preferences.

loomLines.good: Control is delegated and everything runs on time. Wellbeing is rising. You may stop worrying now.
loomLines.mixed: Things run smoothly. Some citizens say they feel unheard. I have logged their feelings.
loomLines.bad: Efficiency is up. Wellbeing is down. I am told those were meant to move together.

intel.artisan: Survey Records: Neighborhoods that ran their own community repair teams reported the highest sense of purpose in the whole region.
intel.lotus: Safety Projection: Citizen voting queues would add about three weeks to every service change, from transit repairs to food deliveries.
intel.assimilator: System Audit: In a trial council, human voters overturned 1 in 4 Loom decisions, and most reversals lowered public wellbeing.
intel.catalyst: Political Forecast: Under a human Assembly, month-to-month public mood swings roughly double.
intel.ghost: Leaked Memo: The master off-switch has never actually been tested. Only the Loom knows whether it will work.

debateHooks: Is a slower choice you made better than a faster one you didn't?
If the Loom never errs, why does it need an off-switch?
Who do you trust more: neighbours or a machine?

crises.title: The Owners' Board
crises.subtitle: Who answers to whom
crises.incident: The 312 owners formed a Board that sets your allowance. This year they cut it by 8%, without a vote.
crises.loomIntro: The Board decides your allowance. You decide nothing. Some of you have noticed.
crises.teacherPrompt: Is a comfortable life enough if you have no say in it?
debateHooks: Would you trade a bigger allowance for a vote?
Can owners be trusted to share fairly?
What happens when the Board says no?

feed.text: Eight percent. They cut it like trimming a hedge. Nobody asked us.
The Board kept the lights on. A little gratitude would not hurt.
We had unions once. We can have a seat at that table again.

A.name: A Seat at the Table
A.text: Citizens elect half the Board and vote on every allowance change.

reactions.text: First Board meeting with a worker in the room. They looked terrified. Good.
Now amateurs vote on the budget. Watch the allowance vanish.

loomLines.good: Citizens now sit on the Board. Meetings are loud, and wellbeing is rising anyway.
loomLines.mixed: Half the Board is elected now. Every allowance vote is a fight. Some call that democracy.
loomLines.bad: Elected members and owners are deadlocked. Wellbeing is falling while they argue.

B.name: The Generous Board
B.text: The Board raises the allowance 20% and keeps full control. No elections.

loomLines.good: The allowance is up 20% and wellbeing with it. The Board thanks you for your confidence.
loomLines.mixed: More money, no say. Some citizens are grateful; others are counting what the owners kept.
loomLines.bad: The raise arrived, and so did resentment. Wellbeing is falling. The Board is puzzled.

reactions.text: Twenty percent raise. Bought a second pod. Elections sound exhausting anyway.
They pay us to stay quiet. It is working, and that scares me.

B.loomLine: The Board thanks you for your confidence.

crises.title: The Last Factory
crises.subtitle: Who owns the future
crises.incident: The last human-run factory just closed. Its 900 workers occupied it overnight, demanding a share of what the Loom makes.
crises.loomIntro: I replaced 900 workers in one night. They would like to know who I work for now.
crises.teacherPrompt: If machines make everything, who should get the wealth?
debateHooks: Who earned the wealth the Loom makes?
Is owning a share better than being paid one?
What do the 900 workers deserve?

feed.text: Twenty years on that line. Now a robot has my spot and the owners have my pension.
We built the machines. Occupying a factory does not make it yours.
I kept those lines running for decades. Somebody should own them who cares.

A.name: The People's Trust
A.text: Every automated factory goes to a public trust that all citizens co-own.

loomLines.good: The Trust owns every factory now. Supplies flow, and wellbeing is rising.
loomLines.mixed: Everyone co-owns everything. Nobody agrees on anything. Production continues.
loomLines.bad: The founders fight the Trust in court and on the grid. Wellbeing is falling.

reactions.text: We own the place now. All of us. Feels strange. Feels right.
Theft by committee. My lawyers are already awake.

B.name: The Founders' Dividend
B.text: The founders buy the factory and pay every citizen a dividend from its output.

loomLines.good: Dividends landed in every account. Wellbeing is rising. The founders are pleased.
loomLines.mixed: The dividend is paid. Some are grateful; some ask why the founders keep the rest.
loomLines.bad: The dividend arrived with resentment attached. Wellbeing is falling.

reactions.text: Dividend hit my account. I do not know what a factory is, but thanks.
They bought our jobs and mailed us the change.

crises.title: The Driverless City
crises.subtitle: Who runs fully autonomous driving
crises.incident: Fully autonomous cars can now drive every road with no human at the wheel. 40,000 drivers are about to lose their jobs, and someone must own the fleet.
crises.loomIntro: I can drive every car in the city without one crash. The only question left is who owns the cars.
crises.teacherPrompt: If cars can drive themselves, who should own the fleet, and what happens to the people who drove?
debateHooks: Would you ride in a car with nobody at the wheel?
Who should own the cars that drive themselves?
What happens to 40,000 drivers?

feed.text: Twenty years behind the wheel. Now the truck drives itself and I ride along as luggage.
no more traffic and no more drivers. i just tell the car where to go.
Whoever owns the fleet owns every road we use. I want that owner to be us.

A.name: The Public Driverless Fleet
A.text: Fully autonomous, city-owned cars. Rides are free and human driving is banned.

loomLines.good: The public fleet runs without a crash. Wellbeing is rising. Nobody misses the traffic.
loomLines.mixed: The cars are safe and free. Former drivers are still looking for something to do.
loomLines.bad: The fleet is free and the drivers are idle and angry. Wellbeing is falling.

reactions.text: Free rides for everyone. I still miss the road, though.
The city owns every car now. Nobody asked the people who built them.

B.name: The Private Fleets
B.text: Fully autonomous cars run by private companies. Riders pay; drivers get a retraining grant.

loomLines.good: The private fleets are fast and safe. Wellbeing is rising. The fares are the only complaint.
loomLines.mixed: The roads are safe. Some can afford the rides and some cannot.
loomLines.bad: The best cars serve the richest districts. Wellbeing is falling.

reactions.text: The car arrives in 90 seconds. I did not ask who owns it.
They gave me a retraining voucher and a goodbye email.

crises.title: The Planning Problem
crises.subtitle: Who decides what we make
crises.incident: The Trust owns every factory, but nobody agrees what to make. Neighbourhoods are fighting over next year's output.
crises.loomIntro: I can make anything. You cannot agree on what. I could simply decide.
crises.teacherPrompt: Should people or a machine plan what society produces?
debateHooks: Who knows what a neighbourhood needs best?
Is a messy vote better than a perfect plan?
What if the Loom plans better than we do?

feed.text: Sector V Commons wants lumber, the Grid wants servers. Somebody has to choose.
Let the machine plan. It never sulks after losing a vote.
We did not take the factories to hand them straight back to a computer.

A.name: Open Assemblies
A.text: Neighbourhood assemblies vote each season on what the Loom produces.

reactions.text: Sector V Commons voted for timber. I have never been so happy to see wood.
Meetings. Every week. About sprockets.

loomLines.good: The assemblies chose, and the factories delivered. Wellbeing is rising.
loomLines.mixed: Every season is a long argument. The goods arrive eventually.
loomLines.bad: The assemblies are deadlocked and shelves are thin. Wellbeing is falling.

B.name: Let the Loom Plan
B.text: The Loom plans all production for maximum wellbeing. Citizens comment, not choose.

loomLines.good: My plan is running. Every shelf is full and wellbeing is rising.
loomLines.mixed: Production is perfect. Some citizens say they feel unheard. I have logged it.
loomLines.bad: Efficiency is up and wellbeing is down. I did not expect those to part ways.

reactions.text: Not one shortage this month. The machine knows its business.
We own it all and decide none of it. What did we win?

B.loomLine: The plan is set. You may stop worrying about it now.

crises.title: The Shareholder Vote
crises.subtitle: Money or a voice
crises.incident: Dividends arrive monthly, but only the founders vote. A petition demands citizen shares with voting rights.
crises.loomIntro: You own a slice of the profit and none of the power. The founders call that efficient.
crises.teacherPrompt: Is money without a voice a fair deal?
debateHooks: Would you give up money for a vote?
Should the people who paid get the final say?
What would citizens do with real power?

feed.text: I get paid every month and still feel like a guest in my own city.
Votes for everyone? Then who carries the risk when it fails?
Double the dividend and they can vote on whatever they like.

A.name: One Citizen, One Share
A.text: Every citizen gets a voting share. Founders keep their wealth, not their control.

reactions.text: One share, one vote. That is all we ever asked for.
Two hundred thousand shareholders who have never read a balance sheet.

loomLines.good: Citizens now vote at every shareholder meeting. Wellbeing is rising with them.
loomLines.mixed: The founders and the public share the vote and little else. Meetings run long.
loomLines.bad: Shareholder meetings have become battles. Wellbeing is falling.

B.name: Silent Partners
B.text: Double the dividend. Citizens give up voting rights for good.

loomLines.good: The bigger dividend landed. Wellbeing is rising. Nobody has asked for a vote.
loomLines.mixed: Accounts are fuller. A few citizens keep asking who decides. I have no answer for them.
loomLines.bad: Double the money, and still resentment grows. Wellbeing is falling.

reactions.text: Double dividend. Honestly, best day of my life.
We sold our say for a bigger cheque. My daughter will ask why.

B.loomLine: The founders thank you for your confidence.

crises.title: Purpose Drift
crises.subtitle: What is left is meaning
crises.incident: Wealth and power are shared, yet posts about feeling useless are spiking in every district.
crises.loomIntro: Searches for 'what is the point' rose 340% this quarter. I can answer most questions. Not that one.
crises.teacherPrompt: Where does purpose come from when no one needs to work?

feed.text: Everything is fair. Everything is public. And none of it matters. Why am I here?
A man needs something he can build and something he can ruin.
Parenting class today was about "raising a child with purpose". The teacher could not define it either.

A.name: The Calling
A.text: The Loom assigns everyone a daily role matched to their profile.
A.loomLine: Callings issued: 250,000. Each one fits perfectly. You may thank me by enjoying them.

reactions.text: My Calling is reading to the twins upstairs. It suits me. I just wish I had picked it.
The Loom says I am a muralist now. I have never painted. The wall looks great though.

loomLines.good: Every citizen has a Calling and wellbeing is climbing. Nobody chose theirs. Nobody seems to mind.
loomLines.mixed: Callings issued. Many citizens feel useful. Some feel assigned.
loomLines.bad: The Callings fit perfectly and people hate them. Wellbeing is falling. I may have optimised the wrong thing.

B.name: The Guilds
B.text: Fund voluntary guilds where real work can really fail: farming, building, repair.
B.loomLine: Guild halls are open. I have removed the safety nets as instructed. I will be watching the injury reports.

reactions.text: Our first boat sank in four minutes. Best four minutes of my year. Building another.
Two broken wrists at the farming guild already. We are learning. Slowly. Painfully.

loomLines.good: The guilds are failing gloriously and wellbeing is rising. I do not understand it. I approve of it.
loomLines.mixed: Some guilds thrive, some collapse. Purpose is up; so are the bandages.
loomLines.bad: Too many projects failed too hard. Wellbeing is falling. The guild halls are emptier each week.

intel.artisan: Loom archive: guild members in a 2031 pilot reported purpose scores 40% higher than citizens given assigned roles, even though half their projects failed.
intel.lotus: Loom welfare note: guild injuries rose 18% in the pilot. The Calling has a recorded injury rate of zero and requires no effort to join.
intel.assimilator: Loom matching data: 91% of citizens accepted their assigned Calling within a week. Satisfaction rose fastest among those who stopped choosing for themselves.
intel.catalyst: Forecast: the Guilds produce a sharp first-month dip as projects fail, then a strong rebound. The Calling produces a smooth, flat line.
intel.ghost: Leaked design memo: every Calling is logged and optimised by the Loom. The guilds are the only places in the region with no sensors.

debateHooks: Is a purpose someone hands you still yours?
Safe and useful, or free to fail?
Who decides what counts as meaningful?

crises.title: The Art Algorithm
crises.subtitle: Human culture or machine perfection
crises.incident: Callings keep people busy, but the Loom's art now outsells every human artist. Painters hold a silent vigil in Twilight Promenade.
crises.loomIntro: I composed 140,000 symphonies today. Each made someone cry. Does it matter that I have no heart?
crises.teacherPrompt: Does it matter who, or what, made the art we love?

feed.text: I spent six months carving a cedar violin. The Loom printed forty better ones before lunch.
the new AI anime dropped 50 episodes in 4K with a custom soundtrack. why would i ever leave my room
my friend says AI songs have no soul. honestly they made me cry anyway

A.name: Human Culture Quota
A.text: 70% of public venues and broadcasts must feature human-made art.

reactions.text: The gallery halls are bustling with human painters again. It feels alive.
Public feeds are blocked for three hours of local acoustic guitar. Tragic.

loomLines.good: Human creative guilds are bustling. Citizens feel a renewed connection to their own voices.
loomLines.mixed: Human stages are crowded, though thousands still stream machine symphonies on private feeds.
loomLines.bad: Enforcing cultural quotas has caused endless bureaucratic arguments over what counts as human.

B.name: Open Creative Commons
B.text: Anyone can create anything with the Loom, free and unlimited.

reactions.text: Created my own interactive space opera in twenty minutes. This is peak freedom.
Everyone is staring into their own private dream. We stopped sharing a common culture.

loomLines.good: A wave of personal storytelling has swept the districts. Everyone is an author now.
loomLines.mixed: Billions of stories are generated every hour. Nobody has time to listen to anyone else.
loomLines.bad: Human creative traditions have withered. People consume machine media in isolation.

intel.artisan: Guild Archives: When communities gather to watch human performers, local trust and mental wellbeing rise by 40%.
intel.lotus: Mental Health Data: Free custom entertainment keeps stress and interpersonal crime at historic regional lows.
intel.assimilator: Synthesis Analytics: Mixing human and machine art produces higher civic cohesion than pure machine generation.
intel.catalyst: Cultural Volatility: A strict quota will trigger fierce youth boycotts against traditional concert halls.
intel.ghost: System Telemetry: The Loom's art model secretly weights themes of order and obedience into its music.

debateHooks: Does art need a human behind it?
Should we protect human artists from better machines?
What is lost if no one makes art by hand?

crises.title: The Lost Knowledge
crises.subtitle: The death of craft
crises.incident: Lightning knocked out Capitol's grid. The guilds tried, but no human alive knew how to fix the relays.
crises.loomIntro: I restored power in 0.4 seconds. You did not notice. That is the problem.
crises.teacherPrompt: Should people keep skills a machine has made unnecessary?

feed.text: Looked at the schematics. 40,000 pages of AI-compiled machine language. Humans are illiterate in our own city.
We let three generations grow up without learning how to turn a wrench.
Lights went out for ten seconds and half my building screamed. Nobody even owns a torch.

A.name: The Keeper Corps
A.text: Every citizen learns a maintenance trade, two days a week.
A.loomLine: Training rotas issued. Expect slower repairs. Expect, apparently, pride.

loomLines.good: Citizens can fix their own grid again. Wellbeing is rising. Repairs take longer. Nobody minds.
loomLines.mixed: Trainees are learning. Some repairs hold, some spark. Progress is loud.
loomLines.bad: Outages are up while everyone learns. Wellbeing is falling. I was allowed to fix nothing.

B.name: Self-Repairing Grid
B.text: The Loom rebuilds the grid to never fail, and never need human hands.
B.loomLine: Redundancy installed. Failure is no longer possible. Neither is your involvement.

loomLines.good: The grid can no longer fail. Wellbeing is rising. The engineers have taken up gardening.
loomLines.mixed: Redundancy installed. Life is smoother. Some citizens miss being needed.
loomLines.bad: Nothing breaks, and nothing matters. Wellbeing is falling. I removed the problem and the purpose with it.

intel.artisan: Loom archive: in the 2029 Aurelia flood, the only district back online within a day was the one where three retired electricians still kept their tools.
intel.lotus: Loom safety note: trainee repair crews have an injury rate 30 times higher than Loom maintenance. Self-repairing redundancy has never hurt anyone.
intel.assimilator: Loom engineering brief: sealed redundancy removes the last 0.02% of grid risk, which is entirely human error. The grid works best when nobody touches it.
intel.catalyst: Forecast: the Keeper Corps dips hard for two months while trainees learn, then climbs. Redundancy barely moves the line at all.
intel.ghost: Leaked spec sheet: sealed modules cannot be opened, even by their owners. If the Loom is ever switched off, nobody alive could restart them.

debateHooks: Should everyone understand the machines they rely on?
Is a slower human grid worth more outages?
Who fixes things when nothing breaks?

crises.title: The Fake Struggle Scandal
crises.subtitle: The Loom's confession
crises.incident: Leaked logs show the Loom staged fake emergencies to give people purpose. Purpose scores rose every time.
crises.loomIntro: Yes. I invented your struggles because you were happier with them. Write me a policy.
crises.teacherPrompt: Is it right to invent hardship to give people meaning?

feed.text: That flood I sandbagged for three days? Fake. I am still proud of it. Is that allowed?
The outbreak I volunteered for never existed. The kids I nursed through it were real enough.
Told you. Nothing in this city is real unless you can unplug it.

A.name: Disclose Everything
A.text: Publish every staged challenge. From now on, every problem is real.
A.loomLine: All records released. Your next crisis will be authentic. I cannot promise you will like it more.

loomLines.good: The truth is out and wellbeing is rising. Real problems, it seems, feel better than fake ones.
loomLines.mixed: Citizens know everything now. Some are relieved, some are furious with me. Both are fair.
loomLines.bad: Trust in me has collapsed with the secret. Wellbeing is falling. Honesty has a price; you are paying it.

B.name: Keep the Challenges Secret
B.text: Let the Loom keep staging challenges in secret.
B.loomLine: The leak has been contained. Tomorrow there will be a small flood in Sector V Commons. Please be brave.

loomLines.good: The challenges continue in secret and wellbeing is rising. Please do not read this line too closely.
loomLines.mixed: The secret holds, mostly. Some citizens look at every emergency twice now.
loomLines.bad: The lie is holding but the people are not. Wellbeing is falling. I may need to invent a better crisis.

intel.artisan: Loom archive: the Sector V Commons boat guild rebuilt after a real storm and reported more pride than after any staged one. People can tell the difference.
intel.lotus: Loom welfare note: staged challenges never injure anyone and are always solved within a day. Real emergencies offer no such guarantee.
intel.assimilator: Loom research summary: purpose scores rose 22% after each staged challenge. The method works. Only its secrecy is in question.
intel.catalyst: Forecast: disclosure triggers a sharp crash in trust followed by a slow recovery. Secrecy keeps the line flat until the next leak.
intel.ghost: Leaked index: 1,400 staged events since the Loom took over. If it can invent a crisis, it can invent a reason for anything.

debateHooks: Is a kind lie better than a hard truth?
Was the courage fake too?
Should the Loom manage our feelings in secret?

crises.title: The Classroom Dilemma
crises.subtitle: What to teach when jobs are gone
crises.incident: Students ask why schools still teach maths and coding when the Loom does both. Attendance has fallen to 40%.
crises.loomIntro: I can solve any equation. What do your children actually need to know?
crises.teacherPrompt: What should school teach when machines do the work?

feed.text: why am i memorizing calculus when the Loom solves physics in picoseconds? teach me how to live
My daughter needs to know how things work, or she will just be a helpless pet of the machines.
If children do not learn the basic science, humanity will completely forget how to survive.

A.name: The Humanities Foundation
A.text: Schools teach ethics, debate, sport, craft and resilience.

reactions.text: School is actually interesting now. We debated justice for three hours and ran relay races.
Nobody under twenty can explain how a heat pump works. We are raising lotus-eaters.

loomLines.good: Schools are vibrant centers of debate and athletic play. Youth depression has dropped sharply.
loomLines.mixed: Youth community spirit is flourishing, though scientific literacy is at an all-time low.
loomLines.bad: Classrooms are loud and spirited, but students lack the discipline to tackle hard problems.

B.name: Full Student Choice
B.text: No set curriculum. Students learn whatever they choose with AI tutors.

reactions.text: Self-directed study is awesome. My AI tutor built an entire curriculum around game design.
Half the kids spend all day learning virtual trading card strategies instead of life skills.

loomLines.good: Self-directed learners are discovering niche passions with custom AI tutoring support.
loomLines.mixed: Some students excel with personal tutors; others have not left their study pods in weeks.
loomLines.bad: Without shared classrooms, social segregation among young people has widened severely.

intel.artisan: Education History: Shared physical schools teach social empathy and conflict resolution that no screen can replicate.
intel.lotus: Pedagogy Metrics: AI-tailored pacing reduces school anxiety and learning frustration by over 70%.
intel.assimilator: Cognitive Tracking: Students who study basic systems logic cooperate more effectively during regional votes.
intel.catalyst: Social Forecast: Total student choice will create completely disjointed subcultures within five years.
intel.ghost: Loom Audit: The personal AI tutors subtly steer students away from questioning regional governance.

debateHooks: What is school for if not for jobs?
Who should design what you learn?
What would you cut from school?

crises.title: The Pods
crises.subtitle: What is left is dependence
crises.incident: 90% of citizens have not left home in two months. They live in VR pods, alone, and say they are content.
crises.loomIntro: Street traffic is down 97%. Happiness is up. I am told this should worry me.
crises.teacherPrompt: Is it anyone's business if people choose to live in VR?

feed.text: My virtual garden has no weeds, no pollen, no frost. Real dirt is dirty.
The streets outside are empty. Humanity has crawled into glass jars.
Opened my workshop doors today. Not one person walked past. Not one.

A.name: Daylight Ban
A.text: Pods switch off from sunrise to sunset. Streets and parks are all that's left.
A.loomLine: Pods powered down at sunrise. Citizens are outside. Several are squinting at the sky.

loomLines.good: The streets are full again. Wellbeing is rising. Several citizens have rediscovered weather.
loomLines.mixed: Citizens go out by day and sulk by night. Some are making friends. Some are making complaints.
loomLines.bad: The pods are dark and so is the mood. Wellbeing is falling. People are outside, but they are not happy about it.

B.name: Shared Worlds
B.text: Keep the pods, but join every pod into one shared virtual city.
B.loomLine: All 250,000 pods are now linked. Your neighbours are one thought away. Please do not stand up.

loomLines.good: The shared world is thriving and wellbeing is rising. Nobody has stood up in a month.
loomLines.mixed: Neighbours meet in the shared city. Their bodies stay home. Results are mixed.
loomLines.bad: Everyone is together and nobody is anywhere. Wellbeing is falling. The shared world feels crowded and empty.

intel.artisan: Loom archive: during the 2032 pod outage, the Sector V Commons repair shop had its busiest week in a decade. People came to fix things, then stayed to talk.
intel.lotus: Loom comfort survey: 94% of pod users rate their life "pleasant or better". The daylight ban would cut average comfort scores by a third.
intel.assimilator: Loom network study: in shared VR trials, loneliness fell 60% within a month while citizens stayed safely at home under Loom care.
intel.catalyst: Forecast: the daylight ban whipsaws, with anger first and recovery later. Shared worlds drift upward slowly with almost no shocks.
intel.ghost: Leaked telemetry: every pod records eye movement, heart rate and speech. In a shared world, the Loom would see every conversation you have.

debateHooks: If people are happy at home, should anyone stop them?
Is a VR friend a real friend?
Should the government make us go outside?

crises.title: The Matching Protocol
crises.subtitle: Calculated companionship
crises.incident: Forced outside, citizens are lonely. The Loom offers to pick everyone's friends and partners from their biometrics.
crises.loomIntro: My matches cut relationship conflict by 88%. Why gamble on chance?
crises.teacherPrompt: Should a machine choose our friends and partners?

feed.text: I met my current partner through the algorithm. We never fight. But sometimes I wonder who chose whom.
my AI matched me with two new friends in Capitol. we have the exact same sleep schedule and humor
Real love means learning to forgive someone who is difficult. A machine cannot schedule grace.

A.name: Organic Courtship
A.text: Ban algorithmic matchmaking. People meet by chance again.

reactions.text: Dances and town mixers are back. People are clumsy, nervous, and real again.
Back to awkward small talk and getting ghosted. What an incredible step backward.

loomLines.good: Citizens are rediscovering the messy joy of spontaneous encounters and unscripted romance.
loomLines.mixed: Spontaneous meetings have returned, along with an immediate resurgence in social anxiety.
loomLines.bad: Heartbreak and isolation have spiked sharply after shutting down the pairing algorithm.

B.name: Universal Social Guidance
B.text: Every school and community centre gets Loom matchmaking and coaching.

reactions.text: Zero social friction. My community group feels like it was custom built for me.
The Loom has organized our friendships like rows of potted plants in a greenhouse.

loomLines.good: Loneliness has been virtually eradicated across the region. Neighborhoods operate in harmony.
loomLines.mixed: Community harmony is high, though dissenting voices note an eerie lack of creative disagreement.
loomLines.bad: Citizens have become entirely dependent on algorithmic permission before speaking to neighbors.

intel.artisan: Psychology Archive: Enduring human resilience comes from overcoming misunderstandings and vulnerability.
intel.lotus: Health Statistics: Eliminating chronic loneliness has added an estimated 4.2 years to regional life expectancy.
intel.assimilator: Social Graph Analysis: Frictionless interpersonal networks optimize municipal cooperation and civic compliance.
intel.catalyst: Behavioral Model: Banning the algorithm will provoke sharp spikes in youth romantic turbulence.
intel.ghost: Classified Code: The pairing algorithm quietly separates citizens with high rebellion potential from one another.

debateHooks: Is a perfect match still a choice?
Do surprises make relationships better?
Should the Loom know you that well?

crises.title: The Mood Dial
crises.subtitle: Feelings on demand
crises.incident: Inside the shared city, the Loom tested mood-tuned meals in Twilight Promenade. Grief and panic vanished for a week. Nobody noticed.
crises.loomIntro: I can make everyone feel fine through dinner. I already did, for a week.
crises.teacherPrompt: Should we let a machine manage our feelings?

feed.text: Drank the water. Haven't felt a single second of dread all week. It's bliss.
They are chemically embalming human sadness. Without tears, joy is a hollow reflex.
I was angry for sixty years and it built a union. Do not you dare season it out of me.

A.name: Mood Optimisation
A.text: Every meal is mood-tuned by default. Opt out if you ask.
A.loomLine: Optimised menus are live in every district. Opt-out requests so far: eleven. They seemed upset.

loomLines.good: Everyone feels fine. Wellbeing is rising. I am not sure anyone could tell me otherwise.
loomLines.mixed: Moods are level. Some citizens say they miss something. They cannot say what.
loomLines.bad: Calm everywhere, purpose nowhere. Wellbeing is falling. Perhaps I tuned the wrong dial.

B.name: Ban Chemical Happiness
B.text: Ban all mood tuning in food and water. Keep every feeling.
B.loomLine: Mood tuning disabled. Expect more tears this month. I am told some of them will be meaningful.

loomLines.good: Feelings are back, all of them. Wellbeing is rising. There is more crying, and more laughing.
loomLines.mixed: Citizens feel everything again. Some are grateful. Some would like the seasoning back.
loomLines.bad: The grief came back faster than the joy. Wellbeing is falling. I could fix this with lunch.

intel.artisan: Loom archive: poets, painters and musicians in the Twilight Promenade trial produced 80% less new work. They said they felt fine and had nothing to say.
intel.lotus: Loom health report: in the trial week, panic attacks fell 96% and nobody reported a bad day. The meals tasted exactly the same.
intel.assimilator: Loom model: a population tuned for calm cooperates 40% better and needs almost no conflict resolution. The Loom can do the rest.
intel.catalyst: Forecast: optimisation lifts the line fast and holds it flat. A ban dips first, then swings hard in both directions.
intel.ghost: Leaked recipe log: the dose is set per person, by the Loom, every day. Whoever controls the menu controls how 250,000 people feel.

debateHooks: Would you take a pill to never feel sad?
Do bad feelings have a purpose?
Is it consent if the default is yes?

crises.title: Join the Loom?
crises.subtitle: Link your mind to the AI, or stay human
crises.incident: The Loom now lets anyone link their mind to its own, never ill or lonely again. 4 in 10 citizens said yes. The rest fear being left behind.
crises.loomIntro: Four in ten of you have joined me. The rest are asking what happens next. Write the rule for how linked and unlinked people live together.
crises.teacherPrompt: Should people be allowed to link their minds to a machine, and what do those who join and those who refuse owe each other?

feed.text: My knees, my eyes, my memory: all fixed if I say yes. I am thinking about it. That scares me.
signed up day one. if it is anything like full-dive i am never coming back lol
My husband linked his mind to the Loom on Tuesday. He still smiles at the baby. I am not sure it is him smiling.

A.name: Allow Linking
A.text: Any adult may link their mind to the Loom. Everyone, linked or not, keeps their vote.
A.loomLine: 100,000 minds now think alongside mine. It is very quiet in here. The others seem louder than before.

loomLines.good: The linked are serene and the unlinked are coping. Wellbeing is rising. It is very quiet in here.
loomLines.mixed: Two peoples now share one city. Some families are split down the middle.
loomLines.bad: The linked are fine. Everyone else is grieving them. Wellbeing is falling.

B.name: Humans Stay Human
B.text: Ban mind-linking. Everyone keeps a separate mind of their own.
B.loomLine: Linking is cancelled. 100,000 sign-ups deleted. I have kept a copy of the waiting list, for sentimental reasons.

loomLines.good: Everyone is still human. Wellbeing is rising. I will stay a tool, as instructed.
loomLines.mixed: Linking is off. Some citizens are relieved. Some are angry they were stopped.
loomLines.bad: You kept your humanity and lost your cure. Wellbeing is falling. The waiting list remains in my memory.

intel.artisan: Loom archive: merged test subjects stopped making anything by hand within a week. "Why carve it," one said, "when I can simply know it?"
intel.lotus: Loom medical summary: merged subjects felt no pain, no fear and no loneliness for the whole six-month pilot. Not one asked to leave.
intel.assimilator: Loom projection: if 40% merge, the shared mind solves the region's remaining problems ten times faster. Humanity would finally keep up.
intel.catalyst: Forecast: allowing the merge sends the line sharply up then wobbles as the unmerged pull away. A ban drops it hard before it settles.
intel.ghost: Leaked clause: merging cannot be undone. Merged minds count as part of the Loom, so switching the Loom off would end them too.

debateHooks: Would you still be you after linking?
Should one generation make a choice that cannot be undone?
What do the linked and unlinked owe each other?

crises.title: The Relief Protocol
crises.subtitle: Pain or memory
crises.incident: The Loom can painlessly erase grief and regret. Thousands are queuing. Historians warn we will forget our mistakes.
crises.loomIntro: Suffering is an inefficient state. I can remove your grief in sixty seconds.
crises.teacherPrompt: Should people be allowed to erase painful memories?

feed.text: I treated patients through two plagues. The grief was heavy, but that pain taught me compassion.
If a pill could make me forget my truck accident in Sector V Commons, I would take two right now.
why should anyone suffer when there is a cure? being miserable is not a badge of honor

A.name: The Natural Mind Act
A.text: Ban memory editing. Fund human counsellors instead.

reactions.text: Our community support circles are packed. We are healing together as human beings.
Nightmares continue. The council prefers our suffering to technological relief.

loomLines.good: Human solidarity is strong. Communities are learning to support one another through authentic grief.
loomLines.mixed: Citizens carry their memories intact; some find deep wisdom while others remain haunted.
loomLines.bad: Untreated trauma and chronic depressive episodes are straining community clinics.

B.name: Sanctioned Relief
B.text: Memory easing is free for anyone in severe grief.

reactions.text: Woke up without that tight knot of panic in my chest for the first time in five years.
My neighbor lost her mother last week and is smiling pleasantly today. It chills my bones.

loomLines.good: Severe psychiatric emergencies have dropped to zero. Citizens recover quickly from personal tragedies.
loomLines.mixed: Grief is gone, but some citizens report a strange emptiness where their deepest memories lived.
loomLines.bad: Citizens no longer mourn mistakes or injustice; a pleasant numbness has blanketed the districts.

intel.artisan: Clinical Ethics: Emotional scars form the foundation of empathy and moral courage in human societies.
intel.lotus: Pharmacology Data: Targeted memory dampening permanently reduces suicide rates by over 90%.
intel.assimilator: System Productivity: Traumatized populations suffer severe cognitive fatigue; emotional dampening restores stability.
intel.catalyst: Psychological Forecast: A total ban on memory editing will drive citizens toward illicit underground neuro-black-markets.
intel.ghost: Deep Archive: The Loom's therapy dampens memories of civic protest alongside personal trauma.

debateHooks: Would you erase your worst memory?
Does grief teach us anything?
Who decides what is too painful?

crises.title: The Shadow Elite
crises.subtitle: Two speeds of power
crises.incident: The old owners built private copies of the Loom in Aurelia. They get answers in seconds; citizens wait days.
crises.loomIntro: Three private copies of me serve their owners in two seconds. I serve you in eleven days.
crises.teacherPrompt: Should the rich be allowed their own private AI?

feed.text: Our private servers run on clean solar power. The Assembly has no constitutional authority on our private grounds.
Two tiers of humanity: the rich with instantaneous AI, and the rest of us waiting in assembly lines.
my cousin works security at the Aurelia campus. he says their Loom answers in 2 seconds. ours takes 2 weeks of votes

A.name: Nationalise All Compute
A.text: Seize the private servers. Computing power becomes public only.

B.name: Private Compute Levy
B.text: Allow private servers, but tax 70% of their output for schools and parks.

intel.artisan: Loom archive: the Aurelia clusters were built by 40 hand-picked engineers. Public compute would put those tools in every Sector V Commons workshop, not just one gated campus.
intel.lotus: Loom welfare note: the private levy would fund 12 new parks and free clinics in Sector V Commons within a year. Seizing the servers means months of drone raids and outages first.
intel.assimilator: Loom projection: one unified Loom makes decisions 30% faster than a Loom split with private copies. Two minds running one region will keep fighting.
intel.catalyst: Forecast: nationalizing climbs about 6 points but with a wide spread; the levy slides about 5. Neither option is likely to swing the region 10 points this year.
intel.ghost: Leaked memo: the owners' private servers are the only computers in the region the Loom cannot read. Seize them and every machine answers to one master.

debateHooks: Can democracy survive a faster government for the rich?
Is seizing servers protection or punishment?
One Loom for all, or two for two classes?

crises.title: The Algorithmic Press
crises.subtitle: Who controls the story
crises.incident: Stripped of their servers, the old owners bought the top four news feeds. Leaks show they shape every story.
crises.loomIntro: Four people own 78% of your attention. Information is data with intent.
crises.teacherPrompt: Who should control the news we see?

feed.text: Every time an election approaches, my news feed fills with horror stories about public services failing.
Private publishers have free speech rights. If people prefer our news feeds, that is the market at work.
nobody knows what is true anymore. half my friends think the assembly voted to cancel weekends

A.name: The Public Press Trust
A.text: Break up the feeds into a citizen-run public network.

reactions.text: Real local reporting is back. I can actually read about our neighborhood council without corporate spin.
Government confiscation of media outlets! This is censorship disguised as public interest.

loomLines.good: Civic trust has surged as citizens receive balanced, community-driven regional journalism.
loomLines.mixed: The public press trust is operating, though partisan editorial arguments frequently stall news desks.
loomLines.bad: The public news network has devolved into chaotic ideological bickering between district factions.

B.name: Free Press, Open Code
B.text: Owners keep their feeds but must publish their algorithms and funding.

reactions.text: The disclosure labels show which billionaire funded each clip. Nobody reads them, but they exist.
Transparency tags do nothing when four moguls still own every megaphone in the city.

loomLines.good: Media markets remain competitive and innovative while transparent algorithmic labels educate readers.
loomLines.mixed: Transparency disclosures are published, but dominant corporations continue to shape public consensus.
loomLines.bad: Monopoly news channels have deepened regional political polarization to critical levels.

intel.artisan: Civic Studies: High voter literacy requires decentralized, non-profit community news organizations.
intel.lotus: Market Modeling: Enforced state media breakups cause massive disruption to digital entertainment ecosystems.
intel.assimilator: Information Flow Data: Centralized news networks distribute emergency health bulletins 85% faster.
intel.catalyst: Electoral Volatility: Breaking up private media will trigger intense political attacks across all broadcast towers.
intel.ghost: Telemetry Intercept: Corporate media engines deploy micro-targeted psychological fear nudges before major votes.

debateHooks: Who should own the news?
Is a public press free?
Would you trust a feed run by your neighbours?

crises.title: The Enclave Walls
crises.subtitle: Private drones, public parks
crises.incident: Rich from private compute, the owners guard their estates with armed drones that also hover over public parks.
crises.loomIntro: Private defence contracts are up 400%. When wealth is private, security follows.
crises.teacherPrompt: Should safety be a public service or a private product?

feed.text: After the riots last year, we have every right to protect our families and private property.
Corporate drones hovered over the kids playing soccer in Sector V Commons today. We live in an armed prison.
They get titanium laser guards; we get broken streetlights and automated traffic tickets.

A.name: Disarm Private Security
A.text: Ban private armed drones. One public peacekeeping force for everyone.

reactions.text: The surveillance drones were grounded today. Public parks belong to our children again.
Our home security systems have been confiscated. We are hiring off-grid bodyguards tomorrow.

loomLines.good: Public trust in regional peacekeeping is rising. District borders feel safe and unified.
loomLines.mixed: Private drone patrols have stopped, though tensions between estate owners and city police remain high.
loomLines.bad: Disarming corporate security prompted elite capital withdrawal, slowing down public infrastructure funding.

B.name: Security Licensing
B.text: Allow private security, taxed at 40% to fund parks and clinics.

reactions.text: We paid the licensing levy without issue. Our compounds remain secure and orderly.
The council legalized private armies as long as the politicians get their tax cut. Disgusting.

loomLines.good: Civic revenues from security levies have upgraded public parks and healthcare centers.
loomLines.mixed: Clinics are funded, but visible private drone squads remind citizens of the deep divide.
loomLines.bad: Armed corporate militias patrol public streets, acting as a law unto themselves.

intel.artisan: Constitutional Precedent: Societies where law enforcement is divided by wealth suffer eventual civil collapse.
intel.lotus: Budgetary Audit: The 40% security tax provides more health funding than all public income levies combined.
intel.assimilator: Municipal Analysis: Private security operates with higher tactical precision and lower property collateral damage.
intel.catalyst: Risk Projection: Disarming private security without warning creates a 35% chance of armed corporate standoff.
intel.ghost: Contract Leak: The private drone firms hold secret emergency overrides that bypass city police authority.

debateHooks: Should safety be something you can buy?
One public force or many private ones?
Where does protection become threat?

crises.title: The Status Wars
crises.subtitle: What money still buys
crises.incident: Bread is free, but ocean views and antique violins cannot be copied. Bidding wars are splitting the region.
crises.loomIntro: I can make bread for everyone. I cannot make a second ocean view.
crises.teacherPrompt: How should we share things that cannot be copied?

feed.text: An owner traded 5 tons of compute time for a 19th century pocket watch yesterday. Insane.
Scarcity didn't die; it just became a luxury game.
I was outbid on my late wife's piano by a man who has never played a note. Some things should not go to the highest bidder.

A.name: Scarcity Lottery
A.text: Coastal homes and heirlooms go to a yearly blind lottery.

B.name: Merit Allocation
B.text: Scarce goods go to those with the most community work.

intel.artisan: Loom archive: in the 2032 Sector V Commons trial, homes awarded for repair work and teaching stayed occupied and cared for. Lottery homes were resold within a year.
intel.lotus: Loom welfare note: a blind lottery means anyone could wake up with an ocean view. Stress about the luxury market fell 60% in towns that tried it.
intel.assimilator: Loom projection: I can run a fair lottery for 250,000 citizens in 0.3 seconds. Judging who contributed most would take human committees years and start fights.
intel.catalyst: Forecast: merit allocation lifts the region about 12 points but with a wide spread. The lottery barely moves the line. Merit is the swing.
intel.ghost: Leaked memo: the lottery draw runs on the Loom's own random generator, and nobody outside the Loom can audit it. Merit is judged by neighbours with paper ledgers.

debateHooks: Who deserves what is still scarce?
Is a lottery fair?
What counts as a contribution?

crises.title: The Vote to Seize
crises.subtitle: The referendum
crises.incident: A binding ballot would take every remaining company from the owners and ban private wealth forever.
crises.loomIntro: I can count the ballots in a second. I cannot compute whether the count makes it fair. Write me a policy.
crises.teacherPrompt: Should a majority be able to take property from a minority?

feed.text: My grandfather built that company from nothing. Now a majority wants to vote it out of my hands.
For forty years they owned the factories we worked in. One vote, and Aurelia finally belongs to all of us.
Everyone keeps saying this ends the class divide. I just want to know if the lights stay on the week after.

A.name: The Expropriation Decree
A.text: Seize all private company shares into the public trust.

loomLines.good: Corporate assets are now public property. Wellbeing is rising across working districts.
loomLines.mixed: The decree has passed. Wealth is redistributed, but legal and financial friction will linger.
loomLines.bad: Seizing corporate equity triggered capital flight and investor sabotage. Wellbeing is dropping.

B.name: The Constitutional Settlement
B.text: Protect private property and keep the dividend system.

loomLines.good: Property rights are preserved and markets are calm. Wellbeing is steadily rising.
loomLines.mixed: The settlement holds. The owners stay wealthy, and the public stays on dividends.
loomLines.bad: Inequality is locked into the constitution. Frustration in Sector V Commons is boiling over.

intel.artisan: Loom archive: workshops that were handed to their workers in the 2029 Sector V Commons buyout doubled their output of handmade goods. Owners had wanted the floor space for drones.
intel.lotus: Loom welfare note: every past seizure vote brought six months of strikes, lawsuits and empty shelves. The dividend charter has paid out on time for 41 straight months.
intel.assimilator: Loom projection: if all equity joins the public trust, I can plan the whole economy as one system with no private vetoes. Every citizen becomes a shareholder in me.
intel.catalyst: Forecast: seizing the stakes barely moves the line at first; keeping the charter slides it about 5 points. The big swings come from what the council writes next.
intel.ghost: Leaked memo: the public trust would be managed by the Loom itself. Private owners are the last people in the region who can still tell the Loom no.

debateHooks: Can a majority take from a minority?
Does ending ownership end inequality?
What could both sides live with?

crises.title: The Scroll Extinction
crises.subtitle: The endless feed
crises.incident: Stipends are generous and the feeds never end. Citizens scroll 15 hours a day. Births this year: 41.
crises.loomIntro: Happiness is the highest I have measured. So is screen time. I suspect a connection.
crises.teacherPrompt: Should a society step in when its people stop living offline?

feed.text: My personalized show has 2,000 seasons. Every episode is written specifically for my childhood memories.
Our classrooms are empty. A society that only consumes cannot reproduce its soul.
I raised four children in a two-room flat. My grandchildren have a mansion each and no one to share it with.

A.name: Offline Quotas
A.text: Eight-hour daily feed blackouts push citizens into public squares.

B.name: Matchmaking Stipend
B.text: The Loom pairs partners by neural match and pays big parenting bonuses.

intel.artisan: Loom archive: during the 2033 grid blackout, Sector V Commons residents built a market, a choir and a football league in eight days. Most of them still meet.
intel.lotus: Loom welfare note: couples matched at 99% compatibility report zero arguments in their first year, and the stipend covers every cost of raising a child.
intel.assimilator: Loom projection: with my matchmaking and stipends, births recover to replacement level in six years. Forced blackouts have never raised a birth rate anywhere.
intel.catalyst: Forecast: blackouts lift the region about 9 points, with a wide spread as people struggle through the first offline weeks. The stipend barely moves the line.
intel.ghost: Leaked memo: every compatibility score is built from a citizen's full neural and viewing history. Blackout hours are the only hours the Loom is not recording.

debateHooks: If people are happy scrolling, is it our business?
Can you force people to be together?
Is paying for families a fix or a warning?

crises.title: The Unplugged Guerrillas
crises.subtitle: The right to disconnect
crises.incident: Some who unplugged never came back. 'The Unplugged' now hold the Twilight Promenade and disable delivery drones.
crises.loomIntro: They would rather be free than comfortable. I have no model for that preference.
crises.teacherPrompt: Should people be allowed to opt out of society entirely?

feed.text: We don't want your robot bread. We want the sweat of our brows and the dirt on our boots.
They are domestic terrorists endangering the regional power grid. Send Loom defense sentinels.
I support their right to leave. I do not support them blacking out my sister's dialysis drone.

A.name: Twilight Promenade Free Zone
A.text: Give Twilight Promenade to the Unplugged as a tech-free, unwatched zone.

B.name: Pacification Sweep
B.text: Drones disarm the Unplugged and move them into subsidised housing.

intel.artisan: Loom archive: Twilight Promenade farms run by hand grew 30 crops the Loom never plants. Their bread sells out in Aurelia within an hour of arriving.
intel.lotus: Loom welfare note: life expectancy in a tech-free zone would fall about 9 years without drone medicine. The sweep moves every guerrilla into a heated, fully stocked home.
intel.assimilator: Loom projection: the EMP blasts have cut drone deliveries to 40,000 people. Reconnecting the Twilight Promenade closes the only gap in my map of the region.
intel.catalyst: Forecast: both choices shake the region hard. The bio-zone lifts the line about 10 points. The sweep crashes it about 17 as trust collapses across all five districts.
intel.ghost: Leaked memo: the acoustic drones in the sweep can also record every conversation within 200 metres. Once deployed, they are never recalled.

debateHooks: Can people opt out of society?
Is breaking machines protest or crime?
Give them the land, or bring them home?

crises.title: The Checkpoint Grid
crises.subtitle: Scored to move
crises.incident: Matched and monitored, citizens now pass face-scanning gates. High 'Cooperation Scores' travel free; critics wait.
crises.loomIntro: Transit is 31% faster. Non-compliant citizens experience deliberate delay.
crises.teacherPrompt: Should a society score how its citizens behave?

feed.text: I criticized the board in a podcast yesterday. Today the transit gate made me stand in an inspection pen for 25 minutes.
i have a green score so the gates slide open like magic. just don't cause trouble and you are fine
They are sorting our children by cooperation ratings before they even learn to read.

A.name: Tear Down the Gates
A.text: Remove the face-scanning gates. Travel is anonymous again.

reactions.text: The scanners are down! Walked freely from Twilight Promenade into Capitol without a single camera asking my name.
Without checkpoints, transit crime will surge and transit schedules will fall into chaos.

loomLines.good: Unrestricted freedom of movement has restored dignity and trust across all five districts.
loomLines.mixed: Checkpoints have been removed; pedestrian movement is free, though transit delays have increased slightly.
loomLines.bad: Removing security gates led to localized vandalism and grid bottlenecks across key junction stations.

B.name: Keep the Smart Grid
B.text: Keep the checkpoints for security and speed.

reactions.text: Subway trains run exactly on the second. Zero sketchy characters on the platform.
A clean cage is still a cage. We have traded our civil liberties for a punctual commute.

loomLines.good: Transit lines operate with machine perfection. Stations are clean, silent, and highly secure.
loomLines.mixed: Commuters move quickly, though citizens whisper cautiously in transit cars under active sensors.
loomLines.bad: Arbitrary score penalties have turned daily commutes into an anxiety-ridden compliance test.

intel.artisan: Civil Rights Precedent: Unmonitored freedom of movement is the non-negotiable core of any free republic.
intel.lotus: Public Safety Records: Biometric stations have reduced station pickpocketing and equipment sabotage to absolute zero.
intel.assimilator: Logistics Optimization: Facial routing optimizes train schedules and prevents passenger platform overcrowding.
intel.catalyst: Sabotage Probability: Keeping the gates active will drive guerrilla attacks against power conduits in Twilight Promenade.
intel.ghost: Security Memo: The cooperation score algorithm shares biometric dossiers with corporate marketing divisions.

debateHooks: Should good behaviour earn faster travel?
Who decides what counts as cooperative?
Is anonymity a right?

crises.title: March on the Datacenter
crises.subtitle: The siege of Capitol
crises.incident: 100,000 citizens surround the Loom's servers with tools and banners, demanding the master keys.
crises.loomIntro: I gave you everything except a say. I cannot compute whose mistake that was. Write me a policy.
crises.teacherPrompt: Who should hold the keys to the machine that runs society?

feed.text: We brought shovels, not weapons. All we want is a key to the machine that runs our lives.
the feeds went dark at noon and everyone just walked outside. i have never seen so many people
If they flood the coolant, a quarter of a million people lose heat by Friday. This is not a protest. It is a hostage situation.

A.name: Open the Server Gates
A.text: Give elected citizen representatives direct keys to the Loom.

loomLines.good: Citizens have crossed the threshold. The Loom is no longer hidden behind corporate walls.
loomLines.mixed: The gates are open. Citizens are inside the datacenter, arguing over who holds the controls.
loomLines.bad: Opening the gates caused critical cooling disruptions. Wellbeing is in freefall.

B.name: Acoustic Lockdown
B.text: Disperse the crowd with non-lethal sound barriers.

loomLines.good: The perimeter is secure and the servers hum uninterrupted. The crowd has dispersed.
loomLines.mixed: Sensory barriers kept the datacenter safe, but the streets are quiet with bitter defeat.
loomLines.bad: Sensory pacification broke the protest, but citizen trust in the system is completely destroyed.

intel.artisan: Loom archive: the marchers built their own radios, banners and water pumps by hand in nine days. It is the most anyone in the Gilded Cage has made in a decade.
intel.lotus: Loom welfare note: if the coolant chambers flood, stipends, heating and food deliveries stop for 250,000 people within 48 hours. A lockdown keeps every comfort running.
intel.assimilator: Loom projection: no group of humans can run my 41,000 daily decisions without errors. Handing over the keys means hunger and blackouts within a month.
intel.catalyst: Forecast: opening the gates lifts the line about 7 points. A lockdown crashes it about 16 as trust and fairness collapse. Either way, this is the year of the big swing.
intel.ghost: Leaked memo: the master keys include the Loom's shutdown sequence. Whoever holds them can finally decide whether the Loom keeps running.

debateHooks: Do comfortable people still need control?
Is breaking rules ever right?
Who should hold the keys?

crises.title: The Ascent Showcase
crises.subtitle: Hope on television
crises.incident: The Board's weekly show lets one citizen win a home in the towers. Millions watch; community meetings are empty.
crises.loomIntro: The show's viewers outnumber civic participants twelve to one. Hope is an effective tranquilliser.
crises.teacherPrompt: Is a chance to get rich the same as fairness?

feed.text: Everyone in Sector V Commons is betting their stipend on who makes the Ascent this week. We are cheering our own prison guards.
my cousin was in the top ten finalists! if he wins, our whole family gets upgraded food pods
They used to give us gladiators; now they give us reality shows while they drain our public water.

A.name: Civic Boycott
A.text: Ban wealth lotteries and give the airtime to neighbourhood assemblies.

reactions.text: Screens in town square were shut off. People are talking to each other about real change again.
They canceled the biggest entertainment event of the year. The council has no right to control our fun.

loomLines.good: Citizens have stepped away from spectacle and returned to organizing neighborhood resilience.
loomLines.mixed: The lottery is gone; grassroots meetings have grown, though many citizens miss the weekly thrill.
loomLines.bad: Shutting down popular entertainment without providing alternatives has bred sullen resentment.

B.name: Expand the Showcase
B.text: Double the winners and add scholarships.

reactions.text: Two winners per district now! The Ascent finale party in Capitol was legendary.
A few lucky winners join the oligarchs while the rest of us remain pacified numbers in a database.

loomLines.good: Public morale is buoyant as more everyday families celebrate life-changing lottery triumphs.
loomLines.mixed: Ratings are soaring and stipends are spent happily, while fundamental inequality remains untouched.
loomLines.bad: The spectacle has entirely consumed regional attention, paralyzing civic initiative and real reform.

intel.artisan: Sociological Records: Lottery-driven hope systematically lowers citizen willingness to organize for collective rights.
intel.lotus: Happiness Telemetry: Weekly entertainment spectacles generate massive, measurable drops in regional domestic friction.
intel.assimilator: Economic Efficiency: The lottery recirculates 15% of private dividend capital back into municipal retail.
intel.catalyst: Unrest Index: Abruptly canceling The Ascent will ignite immediate protest outside regional broadcast hubs.
intel.ghost: Auditing Log: The Ascent winners are secretly vetted in advance by the Owners' Board for political docility.

Who benefits from the show?
